METHOD OF MEASUREMENT OF FLOW OF WATER IN OPEN CHANNELS USING STANDING WAVE FLUME-FALL
0. FOR.EWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 16 March 1971, after the draft finaliied by the Fluid Flow Measurement Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 0.2 Similar to the standing wave flumes, standing wave flume-falls have their application in the measurement of discharge in artificial channels, such as irrigation canals. The standing wave flume-fall can be depended upon to perform satisfactorily as a useful flow measuring device. Its chief merit lies in having only one gauge observation on the upstream as o compared to venturi flumes which require two gauge observations and also in its constancy of modularity relationship even with the sediment deposition in the upstream side. 0.3 Generally, standing wave flumes should be used. Standing wave flume-falls are `used as necessitated by topography ( when there is appreciable fall in water level ) for efficient dissipation of energy downstream. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is `complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or;analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : Z-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

subsequently, for the measurement of flow of water in open channels. The flow conditions considered are limited to steady flows which are uniquely dependent on the upstream head. The submerged flows beyond modular limits which depend on downstream as well as upstream water levels are not considered. *Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised).

2.3 Reflector -- A wall of suitable height built across the pavement at the end of the cistern to ensure the formation of a positive bed roller (a bed ro!ler which will not cause retrogression of levels towards toe ) immediately downstream. 2.4 FlunGnag RatioIt is the ratio of bed width of flume at contracted section ( including piers 1 tn the bed width of the channel upstream. 2.5 Glacis -- The sloping floor below and in continuation crest of a flume. of the raised

2.6 Hurdling - Water flowing over the ton of a baffle with a high velocity like horse taking on a fence. 2.7 Surging - Surging occurs `when the downstream water level is too high and the secondary wave downstream of baffie is drowned. 3. INSTALLATION
3.1 Selection of Site - A preliminary survey should be made of physical and hydraulic features OCthe proposed site to check that it conforms ( or may be made to conform ) to the requirements necessary for measurements by standing wave flume-falls. Particular attention should be paid to the following features in the selection of site: Availability of adequate length of straight channels;

Reasonably symmetrical and regular velocity distribution, Avoidance of supercritical flow immediately upstream; Rise in upstream water levels due to the measuring structure; and Absence of conditions downstream of standing wave flume-falls which may affect working, by drowning, such as by a controlling structure.
*Glossary revision ) . of terms used in the measurement of flow of water in open channels (undo

4

IS t 6062 - 1971 Ifthe site does not possess the characteristics (a), (b) and (c) which are necessary for satisfactory measuring, it should be rejected unless suitable If an inspection of the channel shows that improvements are practicable. existing velocity distribution is regular then it may be assurned that the velocity distribution will remain satisfactory after the construction of the standing wave flume-fall. If the existing velocity distribution is irregular and no other site is feasible, due consideration should be given to the checkzg of distribution after the installation of standing wave flume-fall and to hpCcJve it, if necessary. A complete and quantitative assessment of velocity distribution Complete information about may be made by means of a current meter. the use of current meter is given in IS : 3918-1966*. 3.2 Inrtallftion conditions

3.2.1 General - The complete measuring installation consists of an approach channel, a measuring structure ( standing wave flume-fall ) and The condition of each of these three components a downstream channel affects the overall accuracy of the measurement ( see 3.2.2,3.2.3 and 3.2.4 ) . Installation requirements include such features as precise dimensions of structure, its finish, regular cross-sectional shape of approach and exit channels, influence of control devices upstream and downstream of structures, etc. Once an installation has been designed, affect the basis of design should be prevented. any change which \;ould

3.2.2 Approach Channel - On all installarions the ilow in the approach channel shall ,be smooth, free from disturbance and have velocity distribution as normal as possible over the cross-sectional area. This rnay be Unless otherwise specified in the usually verified by measurements. appropriate sections, the following general requirements shall be complied with: The altered flow conditions due to the construction of standing wave flume-fall might have the effect of deposition of sediment The likely consequential changes in upstream of the structure. the water level should be taken into account in the design. b) The natural stream or river cross-section should be reasonably uniform and the channel should be straight for such a length as to ensure uniform velocity distribution. If the entry to thr approach channel is through a bend or if the flow is discharged into the channel from head regulator through a conduit of smaller -`Code of practice for use of current meter ( cup type) for water flow measurement.

cross-sectional area or at an angle, then a longer lengthof straight approach channel may be required to achieve an even velocity distribution. c) The channel should bc in overall regime, that is, over tne year there are inappreciable changes 3.2.3 The Measuring Structure (Standing Wave Flume-Fall ) - The standing wave flume-fall consists of an a preach transition, a throat,with or withe and baflle platform ( between the glacis out hump, exit transition, a ba ttp and cistern ) for better dissipation of energy and the exit may have either parallel sides or expanding sides ( see Fig. 1 ). The entire measuring structure shall be rigid and watertight, at least, for a length L, shown in Fig. 1. It should be at right angles to the general direction of flow and conform to the dimensions given in relevant clauses 3.2.4 Downstream Channel - The channel downstream of the measuring structure ( standing wave flume-fall ) is usually of little importance, as such, provided.that the standing wave flume-fall has been so designed that it cannot become drowned under operating conditions due to silting, back water effects, etc. The effect of rise in the water level on' the downstream due to silting would normally be immaterial, as far as rating of the standing wave flume-fall is concerned. 3.2.4.1 The altered flow conditions due to construction of the measuring structure (standing Gave flume-fall) might have an' effect of building shoals of sediment downstream of the structure, which in course of time might raise the water, level sufficiently to cause submergence of flow. Any accumulation of sediment downstream of the structure should, therefore, be removed from time to tinrc. 4. MAINTENANCE 4.1 Maintenance of the measuring structure ( standing wave flume-fall ) and approach channel is important to secure accurate continuous measurements. It is essential that ap >roach channel be kept clean and free from vegetation and sediment al, far as practicable for at least the distance specified in 3.2.2(b). The float or gauge (stilling) well and the connection to it from the approach channel shall also be kept clean and free from deposits. The measuring structure shall be kept clean and free from clinging sediment and care shall be taken in `the process of cleaning to avoid damage to the structure. To ensure proper maintenance, periodic inspection at suitable intervals should be made. 5. MEASUREMENT OF HEAD

5.1 General - The water level upstream of the standing wave flumeifall may be measured by any suitable type of a gauge where only spot

measurements are required, and with an automatic recording type of gauge where continuous record is required. Gauge observation should, however, invariably be made so that fluctuations are damped down, such as in a stilling well ta reduce surf&e irregularities. 5.2 Gauge ( Stilling ) Well - The stilling well should be so located as to measure the water level upstream of the sill where there is no curvature of flow, This could be ensured by locating the stilling well intake pipe at a distance of 4 JLW, upstream of the bell mouth entrance where &LM is the maximum value of upstream head over the sill corrected for the velocity of approach. 5.2.1 The stilling well. should be normally vertical and have a minimum margin of at least 15 cm over the maximum water level estimated to be recorded in the well. The stilling well should either br carried on a solid foundation slab beiow the bottom of the well, or when pipe construction is adopted the well pipe may be hung from an under-floor located below the point where the pipe emerges from the bank. The under-floor should extend well beyond the limit of the intake pipe trench on both sides and should be solidly bedded on undisturbed ground. The well dimensions should be large enough ( say 60 x 90 cm ) to permit the bottom of the well to be cleaned. The smallest dimension of the well should be, however, not less th2.n twice the diameter of the float of the recorder as given in the Draft ' Indian Standard specification for water stage recorders ( float type )' ( under pr+ma-Qtion*). It is an advantage to fit more than one intake pipe to the well, the lowest being situated below the lowest anticipated stage flow and the others at suitable levels below normal water levtl. In this way, if during the season of high wi&:.er the lower pipe(s) becomes obstructed and it is uot possible to clean it ( them ) owing to the depth of water, the recorder &li con&rue to operate on the upper intake(s) uutil the water level falls sufficiently to allow access to the lower pipe(s). The upper pipes will be usually accessible for cleaning. It is convenient to provide valves in the intake pipes and install flushing systems to clear sediment from the pipes and if this arrangement is impracticable, means far cleaning with flexible sewer rods should be provided. Further, silt trap may be provided near the end of the intake pipe where i: takes off from the channel in order to retard silting.

Intake pipes should be laid level throughout their length; if they exceed 20 m in length an intermediate inspection man-hole should be constructed. 8. ACCURACY

OF MRASURRMRNT

8.1 The overall accuracy of measurement will depend on: a) the proper selection of site, in particular the characteristics (a), (b) and (c) given in 3.1 are satisfied; b) the correct observance of the installation conditions; and c) the accuracy of zero setting and head measurements. 8.2 With. skill and care in the construction of the measuring structure (standing wave flume-fall), the basic equations and the coefficients are expected to give accurate results. Studies to determine errors are being made. 9. LIMITATIONS 9.1 For Satisfactory functioning of the standing wave flume-fall the ratio D,/D1 should be less than 0.5 ( see Fig. 5 ) where D L = depth upstream over the sill of throat, and For

D B = depth downstream above sill of throat. D,/D, greater than O-5 standing wave flumes may be used.

A'PPEWDIX ( Chse 1.2 )
A TYPICAL A-I. DESIGN OF STANDING

A

WAVE FLUMR-FALL

CRITERLlb. OF DESIGN

A-I.1 The following conditions have to be satisfied while designing a standing wave flume-fall: a) The standing wave flume-fall should work for bulk roportionality between full supply discharge ( FSD ) and 1P 3 full supply discharge ( l/3 FSD ), and b) The fall should be designed with hyperbolic expansion in the cistern.

AUGE )-J
